(CNN) -- Authorities searched a church near the site where an 8-year-old California girl was discovered dead on Monday, hoping to uncover clues that might lead them to her killer.

Mourners have left condolences for Sandra Cantu, whose body was found on April 6 in Tracy, California. The remains of the young girl, who had been missing since March 27, were discovered stuffed inside a suitcase submerged in a dairy-farm pond.

Tracy Police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN's Nancy Grace that he could not elaborate on the specific evidence that led investigators to Clover Road Baptist Church, stating only that detectives had established probable cause sufficient to persuade a judge to sign a search warrant.

Lane Lawless, the church's pastor, told CNN affiliate KCRA that he had been questioned by police for approximately three hours, but maintained that he had nothing to do with Cantu's disappearance or death. "We have fully cooperated with the police," Lawless said. "We have answered all their questions."

Authorities also searched the mobile home park where the girl had lived on Tuesday.

Watch report on the murder investigation »

"Investigators are looking at additional information they received since yesterday [Monday], and hopefully that will lead us to Sandra's killers," Sheneman said. When asked whether his use of the plural indicated that police were seeking more than one suspect, Sheneman replied, "We have no specific suspects."

Watch Sheneman confirm that no arrest has been made in the case »

Sheneman further suggested that the perpetrator was likely familiar with the location where the body was found. Despite having lived in the community for nearly 12 years, he noted that he himself had not known of the site. "Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there," he said.

Watch how the suitcase was discovered »

According to Sheneman, police have not yet named a suspect, even after interviewing hundreds of individuals in connection with the case. "Everyone we speak to right now is being considered a person of interest," he said. "We're not eliminating anyone."

An autopsy was being conducted on Tuesday, though it remained unclear when the findings would be released. "It's going to be some time before we hear from the coroner," Sheneman said. "I can't tell you when that's going to be."

More than ten search warrants have been executed as part of the investigation, yielding what Sheneman described as "a lot" of evidence.

On the day she was last seen, Cantu returned home from school, kissed her mother goodbye, and left to play with a friend who lived nearby. A short while later—dressed in a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings—she set off for another friend's home, according to a family spokeswoman. Police confirmed on Monday that these clothing details helped them identify her body.

# Search of Local Church Yields Evidence in Sandra Cantu Case

**TRACY, California** — Investigators executed a search warrant this week at a Tracy church connected to a Sunday school teacher who has emerged as a person of interest in the murder of 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, whose body was discovered stuffed in a suitcase in an irrigation pond earlier this month.

Melissa Huckaby, 28, taught Sunday school at Clover Road Baptist Church, where Sandra had reportedly last been seen alive. Investigators spent hours combing through the church property, removing bags of items that were logged into evidence and transported to a forensics lab for analysis.

Neighbors and churchgoers watched in stunned silence as crime scene tape went up around the building that had long served as a gathering place for local families.

"This is a place where children play, where they learn about faith," said one longtime member of the congregation, who declined to give her name. "None of us can wrap our heads around what's happening."

Sandra vanished on March 27 near her family's mobile home park. Her disappearance triggered an intensive search involving hundreds of volunteers, law enforcement officers, and search dogs combing fields, canals, and abandoned buildings throughout San Joaquin County. Her body was found eight days later in a suitcase submerged in a pond behind a church-owned property, just blocks from where she was last seen.

The San Joaquin County Sheriff's Department has not officially named Huckaby as a suspect but confirmed she is "a significant person of interest" in the ongoing homicide investigation. Sources close to the investigation, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss details publicly, say detectives are examining a possible connection between Huckaby and the child through the church's youth programs.

Sheriff's spokesperson Deputy Les Garcia confirmed that additional forensic testing is underway on items recovered from both the church grounds and a nearby residence associated with Huckaby.

"We are pursuing every lead diligently," Garcia said at a brief press conference outside the sheriff's headquarters. "Our priority remains securing justice for Sandra and her family."

The investigation has cast a somber shadow over Tracy, a quiet Central Valley community of roughly 80,000 residents that had rarely seen this level of media attention or law enforcement activity.

Sandra's mother, Maria Cantu, has made only brief public statements since her daughter's body was identified, thanking the community for their support during the search and asking for privacy as the family grieves.

"She was full of life," Cantu said in a statement read by a family spokesperson. "We just want answers, and we want whoever did this brought to justice."

Church leadership issued a statement expressing sorrow over Sandra's death and pledging full cooperation with investigators.

"Our congregation is devastated," the statement read. "We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and ask for prayers for the Cantu family during this unimaginable time."

No formal charges have been filed as of Thursday evening. Authorities say the investigation remains active, with additional forensic results expected in the coming days that could shape the direction of the case.

CNN will continue to follow this developing story.

Authorities have released details outlining the timeline of events surrounding the disappearance of 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, whose case drew national attention in 2009.

## The Disappearance

Sandra Cantu, a third-grader from Tracy, California, was last seen on **March 27, 2009**, near her home in the Orchard Estates mobile home park. Surveillance footage captured her walking near a neighbor's home shortly before she vanished. Her disappearance triggered an immediate and extensive search involving local law enforcement, FBI agents, and hundreds of community volunteers.

## The Search

In the days following her disappearance, searchers combed the area on foot, by air, and using cadaver dogs. The small farming community of Tracy mobilized quickly, with vigils held and flyers distributed throughout the region. Investigators pursued various leads while examining surveillance footage from the neighborhood.

## The Discovery

On **April 6, 2009**, Sandra's body was discovered inside a suitcase submerged in an irrigation pond near a dairy farm outside Tracy. The pond was reportedly searched multiple times before her body was found, raising questions about the investigation's initial scope. An autopsy later determined she had been sexually assaulted and suffocated.

## The Investigation and Arrest

Huckaby's daughter had reportedly played with Sandra, and investigators noted a suitcase similar to the one used to conceal the body was missing from Huckaby's home.

Huckaby was arrested on **April 10, 2009**, initially on unrelated charges before being formally charged with Sandra's kidnapping, rape, and murder. Prosecutors alleged she lured Sandra into her home before killing her.

## Legal Resolution

Huckaby ultimately **pleaded guilty in 2010** to first-degree murder and other charges, avoiding a possible death sentence. She was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
